To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ROS are universal signalling molecules that are not only involved in stress response but also in the regulation of many cellular processes, including growth and development.
ROS are not only signalling metabolites in plants and animals, but also that the signalling functions of ROS are not restricted to the activation of stress responses.
ROS are universal signalling metabolites and that all oxidative modifications/damages are involved in signalling.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the role of reactive oxygen species as signalling molecules and their involvement in the regulation of plant metabolism, growth and development.
the molecular mechanisms that underlie the regulation of photosynthesis in response to environmental stress.
the role of ROS in plant and animal cells, and in particular, how the cell uses ROS as signalling molecules to control its own physiology and development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
all oxidative modifications/damage are involved as signalling molecules, and that the term oxidative stress is obsolete.
oxidative signalling is a universal feature of all living organisms and that the oxidative modification of biomolecules is the most common form of signalling in all cells.
ROS are universal signalling molecules and that the term 'oxidative stress' should be abandoned in favour of oxidative signalling.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the oxidative modification of proteins and lipids is an important part of the photoprotective response to excess light, and that the resulting oxidative signals are crucial for the induction of repair.
ROS are involved in the control of all aspects of life.
the ROS signal transduction network is the central hub of the plant's stress response, and that the plant's stress tolerance is a direct function of the efficiency of this network.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ROS are not only involved in damage, but are also crucial for the regulation of many processes.
ROS signalling is not only important for the maintenance of cellular homeostasis, but that the ROS signal itself is the damage, and that the signal and the damage are the same.
ROS are not only signals, they can also be the targets for signalling.
